text.p: China had 145 million illiterates by 1995, or 12 percent of its population, which is expected to become a gerontocratic society before the 21st century, the official Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.

A nationwide anti-illiteracy campaign has reduced the number of illiterate or semi-illiterate people who are aged 15 or above by 36.18 million to 145 million by end 1995 compared with 1990, Xinhua said.
While more people are learning to read and write, the society is becoming gerontocratic.
The average age of China's population has risen to over 33, compared with 28 in 1990, Xinhua said, quoting the State Statistical Bureau.
China, the world's most populous nation with 1.2 billion people, introduced a strict birth control policy in the early 1980s, restricting urban couples to one child each.
The annual growth rate of births in China averaged only 11.6 per thousand between 1991 and 1995 compared with 15.54 per thousand between 1986 and 1990, the agency said.
"Experts said China will be listed as one of the world's ageing societies before the 21st century," Xinhua said.
The segment of its society aged between 60 and 65 would account for 6.68 percent of total population compared with 5.56 percent in 1990, the agency said. It gave no further details.
